title: Circuits that Solve Optimization Problems by Exploiting Physics Inequalities
problem: Traditional digital optimization algorithms (steepest descent, gradient-based methods) for machine learning, engineering design, and operations research are computationally expensive; hardware accelerators for neural network training and inference face scaling limitations.
motivation: By exploiting physics inequalities and physical phenomena, circuit-based solvers can solve optimization problems more efficiently than purely digital methods, with applications across deep learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and speech processing.
method: Physics-inspired circuit design where physical constraints and inequalities naturally encode optimization problem structure, allowing analog or mixed-signal circuits to converge to optimal solutions by exploiting inherent physics dynamics rather than implementing algorithmic iterations.
key_novelty: Direct exploitation of physics inequalities in circuit design to solve optimization problems without explicit algorithmic implementation.
contributions: Applications to machine learning, engineering, operations research
Potential efficiency gains over digital algorithms
